summary: Iteration 8 — Emergent-managed Google sign-in ALONGSIDE existing JWT email/password auth. ALL 6 review scenarios PASS. Skills loaded: ai-testing-core. AI-in-scope this iteration: none (auth-only change; LLM chat = not-in-scope-this-iteration, but verified allowed/blocked at the entitlement gate for Google users). Backend pytest: 10/10 pass in /app/backend/tests/test_google_auth.py — (1) POST /api/auth/google/session with NO X-Session-ID -> 400 and no user created (users count stable); (2) with a bogus X-Session-ID 'bogus-<uuid>' -> 401 and no user created; (3) seeded Google user (auth_provider=google, password_hash=None) + minted app JWT via JWT_SECRET -> GET /api/auth/me returns email=google.tester@example.com; (4) GET /api/billing/status returns plan='trial', trial_active=true, allowed=true; (5) Google user allowed to open SSE /api/sessions/{id}/message during trial (status 200, stream opens); (6) after backdating users.created_at to now-5d -> billing_status.allowed=false and POST /api/sessions/{id}/message -> 402; (7) demo <demo-admin-email-redacted>/<redacted> password login still returns 200; (8) password login for a Google user (password_hash=None) with ANY password returns 401 (NOT 500) — verify_password swallows AttributeError on None.encode() and returns False; (9) POST /api/auth/change-password for Google user returns 400 'Current password is incorrect' (NOT 500) — new None-guard on password_hash works; (10) round-trip change-password on demo user (<redacted> -> <redacted> -> <redacted>) all 200s. Frontend Playwright: (a) /login shows google-signin data-testid in BOTH login and register modes with 'or' divider between form submit and Google button; (b) clicking Continue with Google navigates browser to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsquawk-king-ia.preview.emergentagent.com%2F — verified via page.url capture AND framenavigated listener AND request URL list, redirect query param exactly equals window.location.origin + '/'; (c) AuthContext #session_id path: navigating to <origin>/#session_id=fake-session-abc-123 with no sk_token in localStorage triggers a POST /api/auth/google/session with request header X-Session-ID: fake-session-abc-123; on 401, hash is cleaned (URL becomes /login), no sk_token is written to localStorage, user is redirected to /login — app does NOT redirect to /login BEFORE the exchange; (d) happy path via minted app JWT: setting localStorage.sk_token to the seeded Google user's JWT and loading /, workspace renders with 'TRIAL · 3D LEFT' badge, 'NEW SQUAWK' button, user identity 'Google Tester / google.tester@example.com' in sidebar footer — proves /auth/me + billing/status entitlement pipeline works for Google-provider users end-to-end in the real UI.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py verify_password (line 189-193) correctly returns False when hashed is None (None.encode() -> AttributeError -> except -> False). Confirmed by test: /auth/login with Google user's None password_hash returns 401, not 500. Good defensive code.

server.py change_password (line 431) now guards `not dbuser.get('password_hash')` BEFORE calling verify_password — this means a Google user gets the same 400 'Current password is incorrect' as a real wrong-password attempt, which is user-friendly but arguably leaks less info than a distinct 'no password set' message. UX consideration: consider a targeted 400 message like 'Google-linked accounts have no password. Use "Forgot password" to set one.' — currently the sidebar key icon opens change-password modal for Google users too, which will always 400 with a confusing message. Not a bug, UX polish.

AuthContext.js: React StrictMode causes the useEffect to run twice in dev, so 2x POST /auth/google/session were captured in the invalid-session test. In production build StrictMode is disabled and this is a single call. If desired, guard with a `let cancelled=false` closure in useEffect cleanup to prevent duplicate exchanges (each real exchange consumes the Emergent session_id once).

google_session endpoint (server.py:439): uses asyncio.to_thread + blocking requests.get to Emergent — fine, but consider httpx.AsyncClient for consistency. Also: if Emergent returns 200 with an unexpected shape (no email), backend returns 401 — good defense. Session id is NOT logged (only failures are), no PII leak. LGTM.
Login.jsx line 26: `window.location.origin + '/'` is used exactly (no trailing-slash bug); the redirect param encodes cleanly. No hardcoded URL. Matches auth_testing.md contract.
test_credentials: Demo password user: <demo-admin-email-redacted> / <redacted> (unlimited). Google test user: google.tester@example.com (auth_provider=google, password_hash=None) — mint app JWT with backend/.env JWT_SECRET per /app/auth_testing.md. Real Google OAuth completion is not possible in the harness; validated via seeded-user + minted app JWT path (as instructed by the review request).
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral google.tester@example.com user was seeded to Mongo users collection during pytest session; test fixture deletes it in teardown. After the frontend workspace check I also manually confirmed the user was deleted (delete_one -> deleted:1). Demo mechanic user untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite for Google auth lives at /app/backend/tests/test_google_auth.py — run with `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2) pytest backend/tests/test_google_auth.py -v`. It relies on loading /app/backend/.env for JWT_SECRET+MONGO_URL+DB_NAME via python-dotenv. The seed_admin runs on backend startup and re-syncs <demo-admin-email-redacted> to <redacted>, so the change-password round-trip test is safe (even if it fails mid-test, next backend restart restores). Selectors: [data-testid=google-signin] present in login+register modes; AuthContext at /app/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.js line 12-31 handles the hash. To reproduce end-to-end without real Google: (1) seed user + mint JWT per /app/auth_testing.md, (2) `localStorage.setItem('sk_token', <jwt>)`, (3) navigate to /, (4) workspace loads with 'TRIAL · 3D LEFT'. Do NOT attempt to complete real Google OAuth in the harness.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bug found. Backend guards (400 no header, 401 bad session, 401 not 500 for Google-user password login, 400 not 500 for change-password on Google user) all correct. Frontend redirect target + AuthContext hash exchange + workspace/trial rendering for Google-provider users all correct.
